headline: RapWire 24/7: five verified hip-hop and GTA VI developments — Oct. 2, 2026
body: A five-slide original editorial carousel covers The Game’s Drillmatic marketing lawsuit, the Home Team copyright complaint against Jermaine Dupri and Jacquees, Qobuz’s streaming transparency policy, Mac Miller’s Divine Feminine anniversary release, and fresh GTA VI world and weather details.
rendered_body_text: A five-slide original editorial carousel covers The Game’s Drillmatic marketing lawsuit, the Home Team copyright complaint against Jermaine Dupri and Jacquees, Qobuz’s streaming transparency policy, Mac Miller’s Divine Feminine anniversary release, and fresh GTA VI world and weather details.
caption:
1. The Game (@losangelesconfidential), through 100 Entertainment, sued UMG and Virgin Music Group over the promotion of his 2022 album Drillmatic — Heart vs. Mind. The complaint says a $500,000 recoupable marketing fund was promised but only $179,274.79 was spent, including zero of the $125,000 radio allocation. 100 Entertainment is seeking at least $500,000 and argues the shortfall hurt the album’s commercial run; those are allegations, not a finding.

2. Jermaine Dupri (@jermainedupri), Jacquees (@jacquees) and Mass Appeal are facing a federal copyright complaint from Home Team brothers Van and Patrick Watler. They allege the 2023 song “Pick It Up” copied lyrics and melody/harmony from their 1992 song of the same name. The complaint seeks writer credit, publishing income and damages, but the court has not ruled on the allegations.

3. Qobuz has begun labeling releases it identifies as machine-generated music inside its app. The French streaming service says 60% of streams on the identified tracks are fraudulent and excluded from royalties, while those tracks account for 0.38% of all streams on the platform. The move matters because it puts listener-facing disclosure and anti-fraud enforcement in the same frame.

4. Mac Miller’s estate (@macmiller) released The Divine Feminine (10th Anniversary) with three previously unreleased songs: “Butterflies,” “Grand” and “Channel 13.” The 2016 album debuted at No. 2 on the Billboard 200, and the family is also presenting The Divine Feminine Live on Mac’s YouTube channel. It is a catalog release with new music and a live-archive component, not just a vinyl repackage.

5. Grand Theft Auto VI is getting a richer weather-and-wildlife identity before its Nov. 19 launch. Rockstar’s latest cover-story details describe six Leonida regions, more than 170 animal species, localized storms, persistent puddles and hurricanes. The update matters because it suggests the environment will react and persist around Jason and Lucia instead of acting like a static backdrop.

@Rapwire247
